label: Created things have proper actions through their likeness to the creator
summary: Aquinas argues against denying natural things operations of their own. Actual doing follows on actual being, with God as pure act and first cause as his example. The anti-occasionalist conclusion concerns created things receiving genuine activity. The chapter’s use of particular natural effects is part of the case for their genuine agency.
blocker: This gives an account of why actual created beings have proper activity and challenges an account on which created things are wholly inactive. The route needs actuality at its esse respect to select the same domain or an independently justified extension, and each proper activity must supply an OperationOf witness rather than a bare active capacity.
